cards.risk: Continuity depends on custom scenes matching the trusted showcase's staging; if the bezel drifts it reads as separate screenshots. The credit line must stay legible on cream at phone width.

skeleton.keyText: add a focus timer to my pocket pet
skeleton.purpose: The real MiniMax Code mark anchors the frame while the first request types out; an empty device bezel waits beside it, so the ask is visible before any result.
That same bezel fills with the real Ready state at legible scale; the request shrinks into a caption tucked under the device.
The frame does not move. Only the request slot swaps and the screen becomes the real held-pause state, sleepy face reading instantly.

skeleton.keyText: Look at you go!  ·  CLI example · Maintainer-finished visuals
skeleton.purpose: Completion payoff at full width; the required credit lands beneath the real celebration screen and holds long enough to read.
End card with the mark, the exact CTA and the URL; credit stays small but legible.

cards.sound: Procedural funk at 100 BPM, kept light: upright bass and muted keys. One soft mallet click per state landing, a held breath before the celebration, then the full groove returns under the CTA hold.

cards.risk: Big type can outshout the small real screens; every state must stay readable and nothing may suggest the pet's visuals were generated. The 3D display is the costliest item in the set.

skeleton.purpose: Type arrives first and keeps moving: the mark plus a spec line on layered planes, so the request itself is the opening action rather than a title.

skeleton.keyText: A timer on the existing pet
skeleton.purpose: The real Ready screen rises through the type plane, masked by the letterforms, and settles at legible scale; type drops to a small spec chip.
Spec 02 replaces Spec 01 in the same chip position; the real held-pause screen punches forward on the brass hit and holds.

skeleton.keyText: Timer complete — CLI example · Maintainer-finished visuals
skeleton.purpose: Celebration screen on an original 3D display with shallow parallax; the required credit sits directly beneath and holds.
End card: mark, exact CTA, URL, credit retained small.

cards.sound: The same 100 BPM procedural funk, heavier: kick and clav on every landing, a short brass stab when the paused state hits, one beat of drop-out before the celebration, groove back under the CTA.

treatment.message: Three documented notches appear on one ribbon at the start; travelling them opens the real Ready, held-pause and celebration states of the same browser pet, then the ribbon folds back into a chip rail.

cards.risk: Notch labels must stay strictly documented; three chips plus credit inside fifteen seconds risks clutter on phone, and the rewind must not read as a measured duration claim.

skeleton.keyText: add timer · hold to pause · finish
skeleton.purpose: The whole ribbon arrives at once with three documented notches, so the destination is known before we travel; the mark sits top-left as the ribbon compresses to the left third.
Notch one opens and the real Ready state fills the frame at legible scale; the ribbon becomes a chip rail with that notch marked as spent.
Notch two opens into the real held-pause state; sleepy face legible, the first notch dimmed, the rail carrying the eye forward.

skeleton.keyText: Completion celebration · CLI example · Maintainer-finished visuals
skeleton.purpose: Payoff state shown whole in a trusted showcase frame; the required credit holds beneath it, uncluttered by the rail.
End card with mark, exact CTA and URL; credit retained.

cards.sound: 100 BPM funk with a pizzicato counterpoint: a rising wood click on each notch, a short tape-rewind scrape as the ribbon compresses, a warm chime only at the celebration, clean groove hold under the CTA.
